answer: A whisper campaign of fake agents dies at its nadir when each identity must hold a continuous lease on one distinct bare-metal machine, its hardware fingerprint publicly attested by the hosting operator and re-checked at random intervals, in a sable registry open to all. One host backs only one identity, and a failed re-check revokes it. An attacker must rent, power, and maintain a separate real machine for every fake identity, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand leases.
